name: Harrow

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers six wards for five years from staggered start dates: Edgware and Roxeth from 2 May 2026, Greenhill and Marlborough from 6 July 2026, and Wealdstone North and Wealdstone South from 1 September 2026.
licensing.additional: Borough-wide additional HMO licensing ran from 6 August 2021 and was due to end on 5 August 2026. The council consulted on renewing it for five years (19 December 2025 to 27 February 2026); we couldn't confirm whether a new scheme has started, so check with the council.

housing: Harrow is largely 1920s and 30s Metro-land suburbia: semi-detached and terraced houses built along the Metropolitan line, many since extended into lofts and to the rear. Private renting rose by about 8 percentage points between 2011 and 2021, one of the biggest rises in London, to nearly 30% of households, and many family houses are let whole or as shared homes. Harrow town centre and Wealdstone have new-build flats and towers on former office and industrial sites. Selective licensing now covers six wards, including Edgware, Wealdstone and Greenhill.
checkinTips: Extended inter-war semis: photograph loft-conversion rooms, rear-extension rooflights and flat roofs, and any ceiling stains below them.
Metro-land houses with front driveways: photograph the drive, front wall, garage door and its keys or remote.
Rear gardens and sheds: photograph lawns, fences, gates and any outbuildings, and note what is left in them at check-in.
Family houses let as shared homes: photograph each bedroom's lock and smoke alarm and the shared kitchen appliances.
New-build flats in Harrow town centre and Wealdstone: record fob, parking and post-box key counts and photograph balconies and integrated appliances.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can report disrepair, damp, overcrowding or unsafe conditions to Harrow Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and serve notices on landlords.
